title_ar: شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه الشريط الثالث
title_en: Commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory — tape three
body_ar: قال "وترد صيغة الأمر والمراد به الإباحة أو التهديد أو التسوية أو التكوين" يقصد أن صيغة الأمر قد ترد لغير المعنى الأصلي لقرينة تدل على ذلك ، فقد ترد للإباحة كقول الله تعالى: (وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا) فاصطادوا هنا لا تدل على الوجوب وإن كانت صيغة أمر ولا تدل أيضا على الندب بل تدل على الإباحة ، وكذلك قد ترد صيغة الأمر للدلالة على التهديد فلا يقصد بها حينئذ الأمر ، كقول الله تعالى: (قل تمتعوا فإن مصيركم إلى النار) فليس هذا أمرا بالتمتع على حقيقته بل المقصود به التهديد ومثله (فمن شاء فليؤمن ومن شاء فليكفر إنا أعتدنا للظالمين نارا) ، فهذا للتهديد ، وكذلك التسوية وهي التسوية بين الفعل والترك وذلك مثل قول الله تعالى: (فاصبروا أو لا تصبروا سواء عليكم) فاصبروا هنا ليس الأمر فيها للوجوب بل هو للتسوية بدلالة ما بعدها ، فالقرينة المقالية اقتضت صرف الأمر عن معناه الأصلي ، أو للتكوين وهو الإيجاد لقول الله تعالى: (كونوا قردة خائسين) فكونوا هنا ليست الأمر فيها للوجوب وإنما هو للتكوين والقرائين أكثر مما ذكر بل هذه أمثلة للقرائن ومثلها في العكس أيضا للنهي فقد يرد النهي على غير ما هو له، قد يرد للكراهة وقد يرد للتهديد ونحو ذلك..
body_en: He said: "And the form of the imperative occurs while what is meant by it is permissibility, or a threat, or equivalence, or bringing into being." He means that the form of the imperative may occur for other than its original meaning, because of an indication pointing to that. It may occur for permissibility (ibāḥah), as in God Most High's words: (And when you have left the state of pilgrim consecration, then hunt) — "then hunt" here does not indicate obligation, even though it is the form of an imperative, and it does not indicate recommendation either; rather it indicates permissibility. Likewise, the form of the imperative may occur to indicate a threat, so that a command is not meant by it in that case, as in God Most High's words: (Say: enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire) — this is not a command to enjoy oneself in the true sense; rather what is meant by it is a threat. And the like of it: (So whoever wishes, let him believe, and whoever wishes, let him disbelieve; We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire) — this is for a threat. Likewise equivalence, which is equivalence between doing and leaving undone, as in God Most High's words: (So be patient or be not patient; it is the same for you) — "be patient" here, the command in it is not for obligation, but is for equivalence, by the indication of what follows it; the verbal indication required that the imperative be turned away from its original meaning. Or for bringing into being, which is causing to exist, as in God Most High's words: (Be apes, despised) — "be" here, the command in it is not for obligation, but is for bringing into being. The indications are more than those mentioned; rather these are examples of indications. And the like of them, conversely, for the prohibition also: the prohibition may occur for other than what it is set for — it may occur for dislikedness, and it may occur for a threat, and the like of that..

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on al-Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni, a short primer on legal theory. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 649–652 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and tape two does not appear anywhere in the range 601–652.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

THE FIVE RULINGS ARE AT ISSUE THROUGHOUT THIS RECORD and the fixed renderings have been applied exactly: ibāḥah as permissibility, wujūb as obligation, nadb as recommendation, karāhah as dislikedness. The Sheikh's whole point is that an imperative form does not by itself establish obligation, so a slip in any of these four would invert the lesson.

'Indication' renders qarīnah, a contextual pointer that turns a form away from its primary meaning; 'the verbal indication' renders al-qarīnah al-maqāliyyah, one arising from the wording itself as against one arising from the situation.

'Equivalence' renders taswiyah, the case where doing and not doing are put on the same footing; 'bringing into being' renders takwīn, God's creative command, which is not addressed to a moral agent at all.

The source uses round brackets for Qur'anic quotation in this record, where other records in the range use brace brackets. body_ar preserves the source's brackets; body_en uses round brackets to match. The house style's brace brackets have not been imposed, because the inconsistency is itself evidence of how these records were assembled.

The record opens with a bare 'He said' and no doxology, so the beginning of the lecture is not published; it is not marked critical_for_display because the passage that is published is a self-contained explanation with no unanswered question.
